item.title: Voting Ends in Bangladesh With Steady Turnout in Calm, Festive Atmosphere
item.description: Around 47.9 percent of voters had cast their votes by 2 p.m. today, according to the Election Commission.

item.title: Will India’s Kaladan Project in Myanmar Meet the 2027 Deadline?
item.description: A 109 km stretch in Myanmar’s Chin state remains to be completed. Difficult terrain, inclement weather and violent conflict are some of the challenges ahead.

item.title: Bipartisan Meeting With South Korea’s President Canceled After Opposition Leader Skips Talks
item.description: An hour before the luncheon, the leader of People Power Party abruptly canceled, demonstrating his party’s strong antagonism toward the president and dashing hopes for bipartisanship.

item.title: China’s Advance in Guatemala
item.description: Despite a lack of diplomatic relations, Beijing has been remarkably successful in expanding its economic and even political influence in Guatemala.

item.title: Security Shakeup in Kyrgyzstan Continues to Unfold
item.description: The Border Service has been taken out from under the GKNB and at least five people who signed a letter calling for early presidential elections have been detained.

item.title: Pro-Taiwan or Anti-China? Parsing US Public Support for Defending Taiwan
item.description: Most Americans support the defense of Taiwan. Is this motivated more by positive views of Taiwan or anti-China sentiment?

item.description: Forceful territorial revisionism is unlikely – but China is pursuing its interests in Siberia by other means.

item.description: Takaichi’s tenure got off to a promising start with South Korea, but concerns remain that Japan’s rightward shift might upend the relationship.

item.title: From the Peninsula to the Indo-Pacific: The Rebirth of South Korea’s Marines
item.description: The quasi-fourth service overhaul is long overdue. But without expanded regional roles, Seoul risks turning a historic reform into an expensive exercise in symbolism.

item.title: Is China Conducting Secret Nuclear Weapons Tests?
item.description: A U.S. official suggested in recent comments that Beijing conducted a test back in the summer of 2020. So why is the Trump administration bringing this up now?
